compiled_state.description:
## Summary

Bring rebar's CI **coverage and supply-chain practice** in line with popular,
actively-maintained Python OSS projects (Django, Pydantic, pytest, urllib3, cryptography)
**without materially increasing Gerrit Verified gate latency**. This epic actions the
dispositioned findings of the OSS CI-practice research (research ticket
`81fd-c98b-9ca2-4a73`, resentful-titanite-viper, which this epic **supersedes**), plus the
`gerrit-verify` wall-clock investigation session logs (`ae66-91be-df56-40ed`,
`f389-657d-4c03-4e5f`) and epic `ce0e-f618-a2a4-4ee4`.

All findings below were re-verified against current `origin/main`. The design principle is
**value per minute of added hot-path latency**: adopt zero/near-zero-latency practice gaps on
the Verified gate, push everything with real cost to the scheduled sweep against `origin/main`,
and treat the single genuinely-latency-adding item (CodeQL gating) as an explicit owner
decision rather than an auto-adoption.

## Context / Problem

The last round of latency work (epic ce0e, stories A/C, the macOS exit-5 regression fix
`ad4a-f598-39f0-474d`) optimized runtime. It did **not** close a set of *practice* gaps where
rebar is behind the comparison set — several of which cost **zero** hot-path minutes and one of
which is an outright inconsistency (a security file that claims a protection it does not have):

1. **Zizmor is scoped to `release.yml` only** (`Makefile:243-244`; `RELEASE_WORKFLOW` is the
   sole audited target). The workflow that holds the SSH credential casting the authoritative
   `Verified` vote — `gerrit-verify.yaml` — and its reusable callee `_build-and-test.yml` are
   **not** audited by zizmor. `make lint` already installs and runs zizmor (`[dev]` extra), so
   widening the target set is a Makefile-argument change with **no** added hot-path latency.
2. **The SHA-pin claim is partially false.** `gerrit-verify.yaml:21` asserts "All third-party
   actions are SHA-pinned (tag in trailing comment)", but `actions/setup-python@v7`
   (`gerrit-verify.yaml:76,175`) and both `actions/checkout@v7` and `actions/setup-python@v7`
   throughout `_build-and-test.yml` (lines 50,58,249,257,319,328) use **mutable** tags. A false
   protection claim in a security-relevant, vote-casting file is worse than an accurate absence.
3. **`twine check dist/*` runs only at release**, not pre-merge. `_artifact-probe.yml` already
   builds and installs the wheel/sdist; metadata validation there costs **seconds** and catches
   packaging-metadata defects before merge instead of at publish.
4. **Coverage practice.** urllib3 and cryptography enforce ~100% branch coverage; rebar enforces
   a 70% floor. The research (81fd) **deferred raising the global floor** with sound reasoning
   (rebar's targeted mutation testing is stronger evidence than raw coverage, and a forced global
   percentage buys low-value tests). The actionable OSS-aligned coverage step is **diff coverage
   on changed lines**, not a blunt global-floor raise.
5. **Breadth practices with real cost** — intermediate Python versions, Windows, pre-release
   interpreters, dependency lower-bound resolution, external doc link checking, and the full
   macOS suite — belong on the **scheduled sweep**, giving the coverage without hot-path latency.

## Approach

Decompose into independently reviewable child stories, each landed through Gerrit under its own
plan and its own acceptance criteria (this epic is the umbrella; per research 81fd AC-2, each
adopted item becomes its own ticket). Group by latency cost:

**Tier 1 — hot-path, zero/near-zero added latency (adopt on Gerrit Verified):**
- **S1 — Widen zizmor beyond `release.yml`.** Audit all workflows (at minimum `gerrit-verify.yaml`
  + `_build-and-test.yml`, the vote-casting critical path). Runs inside `make lint`; no new job,
  no hot-path minutes. Reconcile any findings zizmor surfaces (this may overlap with S2).
- **S2 — Make the SHA-pin claim true.** SHA-pin the remaining mutable `@v7` refs
  (`actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-python`) across `gerrit-verify.yaml` and
  `_build-and-test.yml` with a trailing version comment, matching the already-pinned actions
  (e.g. `checkout@9c091bb…  # v7.0.0`, `setup-uv@ae62891…`). If any ref is intentionally left
  mutable, correct the line-21 claim instead. Zero latency.
- **S3 — `twine check dist/*` in `_artifact-probe.yml`.** Validate distribution metadata pre-merge.
  Seconds.
- **S4 — Diff coverage on changed lines.** Add a diff-coverage report/threshold over the lines a
  change touches, using the coverage data the Ubuntu cell already collects (near-zero added
  latency). This is the OSS-aligned coverage improvement, in place of raising the global floor.

**Tier 2 — scheduled sweep against `origin/main` (no hot-path cost):**
- **S5 — Extend the periodic sweep** with: intermediate Python (3.12/3.13 — coordinate with the
  Python-matrix work so gate = oldest+newest, sweep = intermediates), Windows compatibility,
  pre-release interpreters (3.15-dev, free-threaded 3.14t) as **non-blocking**, dependency
  **lower-bound** resolution (the lockfile proves one resolution works, not that declared floors
  do), external documentation link checking, and the **full** macOS suite. Each non-blocking so a
  sweep failure never gates a merge but is visible to the owner.

**Flagged for an explicit latency decision (NOT auto-adopted):**
- **CodeQL on the exact Gerrit refspec + `vote.needs`.** Today `codeql.yml` triggers on
  `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch` only, so a CodeQL-detectable defect can earn `Verified +1`.
  urllib3 runs CodeQL per-PR. This is the **one** item that adds real pre-merge minutes; whether
  that trade is worth it is the CI owner's call. Default recommendation: keep it scheduled/
  non-gating unless the owner opts in. Captured here so the decision is explicit, not implicit.

**Explicitly deferred, with reasoning (carried forward from 81fd):**
- Raising the 70% branch-coverage floor toward 100% — mutation testing is the stronger oracle;
  S4 (diff coverage) is the better first step.
- Downstream-consumer / integration testing — premature until public integrations exist.

## Scope

Epic / umbrella: this ticket carries the plan and the disposition of every research finding; the
code changes live in child stories S1–S5 (+ the CodeQL decision), each raised, planned, reviewed,
and landed on its own. No code change lands under this epic id directly. Latency budget: Tier-1
items must add no measurable hot-path minutes (S1/S2 run under existing `make lint`; S3 is
seconds; S4 reuses already-collected coverage data). Tier-2 items add zero hot-path cost by
construction (scheduled lane).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] S1 raised, landed: zizmor audits `gerrit-verify.yaml` + `_build-and-test.yml` (verified by
      the widened `make lint` target and a green zizmor run over those files).
- [ ] S2 raised, landed: every third-party action ref in `gerrit-verify.yaml` and
      `_build-and-test.yml` is SHA-pinned with a version comment (or the line-21 claim corrected),
      so the file's SHA-pin assertion is true.
- [ ] S3 raised, landed: `_artifact-probe.yml` runs `twine check dist/*` pre-merge.
- [ ] S4 raised, landed: a diff-coverage check reports (and optionally thresholds) coverage on
      changed lines, reusing the Ubuntu cell's existing coverage data with no material added
      latency.
- [ ] S5 raised, landed: the scheduled sweep covers intermediate Python, Windows, pre-release
      interpreters (non-blocking), dependency lower-bound resolution, external doc link checking,
      and the full macOS suite — none of which gate a merge.
- [ ] The CodeQL-gating latency decision is put to the CI owner and dispositioned (adopt as a
      gate / keep scheduled / reject), recorded as a comment here.
- [ ] Each Tier-1 story confirms, in its own plan, that it adds no measurable Gerrit Verified
      hot-path latency (the epic's central constraint).
compiled_state.title: CI practice & coverage parity with mainstream Python OSS, latency-neutral
